newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon lifts curfew on Anglophone province.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon lifts curfew on Anglophone province.

text.p: The governor of Cameroon's volatile English-speaking Northwest Province lifted an overnight curfew there on Thursday, three months after it was imposed following a spate of bloody attacks on security forces.
Governor Fai Yengo Francis said the lifting of the curfew followed a return to relative peace in the province during the intervening period, including during a parliamentary election.
"The 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew has been lifted as from today. All security forces are called upon to strictly respect this order," Fai Yengo said in a written order.
Police blamed the attacks, which killed three paramilitary gendarmes and several civilians, on Anglophone separatists.

President Paul Biya's Cameroon People's Democratic Rally (RDPC) won a crushing majority in the May 17 parliamentary election, which the opposition says was rigged. It now holds 109 of the 180 seats national assembly seats.
The opposition Social Democratic Front of Anglophone leader John Fru Ndi won 43 seats, the remainder are divided among five other parties.
The SDF won 19 of the 20 seats in the Northwest Province. Its legislators have entered parliament despite an initial boycott threat.
Biya, who took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982, seeks re-election in October. He narrowly defeated Fru Ndi in the 1992 election, which the opposition says was also rigged.
